title: Sell Mineral Rights in Deemston, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Deemston, PA | Washington County
metaDescription: Deemston sits near the West Virginia line in Washington County's active Marcellus footprint. We buy PA mineral and royalty interests directly, cash, no broker.
heroLead: Deemston is a small former coal-patch borough near the West Virginia line, and the deeds here often carry the same layered coal-then-gas history as the rest of southern Washington County.
intro: Families near Deemston have told us the same thing more than once: they knew their land had been mined for coal generations ago, but nobody in the current generation could say for certain whether the family still held any oil and gas rights underneath. That uncertainty is common in this part of Washington County, where patch towns and coal camps left behind deeds that split mineral estates in ways that don't always match what's carved into local memory.
We do the work of tracing that history before making an offer, so you know exactly what you're selling, not only what you think you might own.

sections.heading: Border-Country Coal Patch History
paragraphs: Deemston sits close enough to West Virginia that some old land grants and mineral conveyances in this area reference boundary lines and neighboring landowners across the state line. Combined with the coal-patch history common to southern Washington County, that can mean a Deemston-area chain of title runs through several separate mineral severances before reaching the present day.
This is detailed work, and it's work we do ourselves rather than asking you to hire a title company before we'll even talk to you.

sections.heading: Wet-Gas Core, Even This Far South
paragraphs: Southern Washington County remains part of the broader Marcellus wet-gas fairway that's drawn Range Resources and other operators for years. Deemston-area acreage sits within reach of that activity, though as always, whether a specific tract has been leased or drilled depends on the section, not only the general county reputation.
We look at what's actually happened near your parcel before discussing value, rather than leaning on the county's overall track record.

sections.heading: What a Post-Production Deduction Actually Looks Like
paragraphs: If your family has an active lease near Deemston, you've likely seen gathering, compression, or marketing fees taken off your royalty statement. That's legal under most standard Pennsylvania leases unless yours specifically prohibits it, and it's a common source of frustration for owners who expected a bigger check. We'll look at your actual statement and tell you if the deductions look typical for this area.

faqs.question: My family's coal was mined out generations ago near Deemston. Could we still own gas rights?
faqs.answer: Possibly. It depends on exactly how the original coal severance was worded. We trace the recorded chain of title to find out rather than guessing.

faqs.question: Is Deemston close enough to active drilling to matter?
faqs.answer: It sits within southern Washington County's broader wet-gas footprint, though we always check activity at the specific parcel level before discussing value.

faqs.question: Why is my royalty check smaller than I expected?
faqs.answer: Usually post-production cost deductions like gathering and compression fees, which are typically legal unless your specific lease bars them. Send us your statement and we'll look at it honestly.
